title: The Roundworm Reference Genome: WBcel235 (ce11)
description: The Roundworm reference genome (Caenorhabditis elegans, assembly WBcel235 (ce11)) spans approximately 100.3 Mb across 6 (I, II, III, IV, V, X) chromosomes, encoding approx 20,300 protein-coding genes (estimate). This record is the assembly-level overview: the anchor for the deterministic scale chromosome -> gene -> protein product -> pathway -> trait used across this database. REFERENCE GENOME ONLY: a public consensus assembly, never any real person's private genetic data. In the Signature framework this locus is read as a deterministic instruction in the organism's living program: address, operation, and output are fixed by the reference assembly, and every Signature reading stays anchored to the public reference fact.
how_it_works: Genome assembly stitches long sequencing reads into chromosome-scale scaffolds, annotates genes by homology and experiment, and publishes the consensus coordinates everyone references. All records in this database hang off these coordinates deterministically. In the Signature framework this locus is read as a deterministic instruction in the organism's living program: address, operation, and output are fixed by the reference assembly, and every Signature reading stays anchored to the public reference fact.
key_points: Assembly WBcel235 (ce11): the public reference coordinates.
Size approximately 100.3 Mb; 6 (I, II, III, IV, V, X).
Gene content: approx 20,300 protein-coding genes (estimate).

description: From Genome to Phenome (Roundworm). the phenome is the genome read out through development and environment; identical reference coordinates produce comparable phenotypes, which is why model-organism genetics transfers to human medicine. In the Signature framework this locus is read as a deterministic instruction in the organism's living program: address, operation, and output are fixed by the reference assembly, and every Signature reading stays anchored to the public reference fact.
how_it_works: Scaling walks the ladder deterministically: pick a level, apply its rules, land on the next level. The generator ladder ranks are simple -> most competitive -> mix-and-match -> unmade -> top-notch -> future grade -> god mode. In the Signature framework this locus is read as a deterministic instruction in the organism's living program: address, operation, and output are fixed by the reference assembly, and every Signature reading stays anchored to the public reference fact.
key_points: Deterministic: same level, same rules, same result.
Generator bound: stops at 10^15 records or complete-with-reason.
standards: Scaling claims are structural, not empirical, and labeled as such
citations: JAH Databases genome lane design notes

provenance: JAH Databases genome lane (r18); public reference assembly facts; nucleotide examples are synthetic representative motifs, never real reference sequence and never any individual genome.
